asr.full_text: How to register and fund your MIRRA Trading International Account You will need the referral link of the person who invited you to join MIRRA Trading International. It will look something like this. Click on that link and you will be taken to the registration screen. Your sponsor's user name will be displayed in the sponsor information section. Next you will see that auto-placement is displayed. Please check with your Sponsor whether you should select the left or right hand position. If you don't make a selection you will automatically go into your sponsor's team lags. Enter a username. The system will tell you if the username is available and a password. Fill in your personal information. Name surname email address valid mobile number and then choose your country from the drop-down list read the terms and conditions and then click I have read and accepted the terms and conditions once you have done this click on the register button a screen will come up with a confirmation message which will confirm your login details. You will also receive an email from Mirror Trading International, confirming your registration. If you found this email in your spam folder, you can inform your system that it is not spam and you'll be able to receive other emails from the company. Now that you have your login details, please log into the back office at mymticlub.com. Then, click on the profile button at mymticlub.com, then click on the profile button in the menu on the left. Please update your personal details and upload your proof of identity. Once you have done this you can click the update button. Adding funds to your Meritrading International pool account. Click on the wallet section on the left, a roll-down will appear. Click on add funds. The payment information screen will appear. You can either scan the QR code or carefully copy the Bitcoin address to your wallet. Make the payment by sending the bitcoin remember some wallets require you to verify the payment via e-mail. Fill in the details. The exact amount of Bitcoin you sent. Enter the blockchain transaction ID or TX ID. Upload the proof of payment screenshot. Then click submit. Once the admin has confirmed your Bitcoin transfer, it will appear in your trading account. In this case your dashboard will that you're a paid member. Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades. You can also log into your back-office to see these results and your statements. Click the view option to see your daily statement. That is your account and how to see the results from daily trading. Should you wish to view your new trading account results and your daily trading statement. That is your account, and how to see the results from daily trading. Should you wish to refer your friends, you can send them your registration link, or you can help them register, by clicking the downline registration link. For more information please contact the person who sent you this video

textual.context: Presented as an instructional account-registration and funding tutorial; whether it is intended as a promotion or only a demonstration is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised trading-account status and recurring trade-result statements are linked to the requested Bitcoin transfer and submission of payment verification, warranting later assessment of the offer and transaction flow.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish whether any returns occurred, whether the account or organization is legitimate, or whether viewers experienced loss.

textual.observation: The registration process requests personal information and an uploaded proof-of-identity document before the account can be updated.

evidence.quote: Fill in your personal information. Name surname email address valid mobile number and then choose your country from the drop-down list
Please update your personal details and upload your proof of identity.

textual.context: Described as part of the account-registration and account-management instructions; the source does not explain how the information is handled.
textual.potential_relevance: Collection of contact and identity information is tied to registration for the account that the tutorial later instructs viewers to fund with Bitcoin, making the requested data flow relevant for later review.
textual.limitations: The records do not show the actual form, identify the data recipient, or establish whether the information request is unusual or improperly handled.

visual.observation: The sampled frames show an instructional sequence titled “How to Register and fund your MTI Account” under Mirror Trading International branding.
visual.context: Visible context is an instructional or tutorial-style presentation; promotion versus neutral discussion is unclear from the sampled frames alone.
visual.potential_relevance: The branded account-registration and funding instruction links an identity/brand presentation to viewer actions involving account setup and funding.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish who produced the video, whether the brand identity is authorized, or whether any viewer completed registration or funding.

visual.observation: The sign-up form displays sponsor information, login creation fields, and personal information fields including name, email address, mobile number, and country.
visual.context: The form appears within a step-by-step account registration demonstration.
visual.potential_relevance: The registration flow links a requested account-creation action to collection of personal contact data and sponsor placement information.
visual.limitations: The frames do not show form submission, data storage, consent terms, or the full terms and conditions.

visual.observation: A registration confirmation screen shows a username, masked password, and a “Replicated Link” beginning with “https://mymticlub.com/...” for the registered user.
visual.context: The screen is presented after registration in the tutorial sequence.
visual.potential_relevance: The confirmation links account creation to a user-specific replicated link, which may be relevant where referral or recruitment steps are part of the observed flow.
visual.limitations: The frame does not establish how the replicated link is used, whether it is shared, or any outcome from using it.

visual.observation: A back-office profile page shows fields for contact number, BTC address, date of birth, gender, ID number, and an “Upload ID Proof” file chooser.
visual.context: The profile page is shown inside the account back office interface.
visual.potential_relevance: The account setup flow links participation to requests for identity-related information and an ID proof upload.
visual.limitations: The frame does not show any file being uploaded, verification result, privacy policy, or how submitted information is handled.

visual.observation: A payment information page for a named user displays a Bitcoin wallet selector, a Bitcoin QR code, a Bitcoin amount field, a transaction ID/TXID field, an upload proof-of-payment file chooser, and a submit button.
visual.context: The payment page appears during the account-funding portion of the tutorial.
visual.potential_relevance: The funding flow links a requested transfer-related action to a Bitcoin destination, QR code, transaction ID entry, proof-of-payment upload, and submission step.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames cannot verify the QR code contents, the wallet owner, whether any transaction occurred, or whether funds were received.

visual.observation: After the payment sequence, a dashboard shows “Paid Member,” a “Trading Pool Balance” in BTC and USD, and a trading bonus report with entries marked paid and percentage-based trading results.
visual.context: The dashboard and report are shown as part of the same account tutorial sequence after funding-related frames.
visual.potential_relevance: The displayed paid membership status and trading-bonus/balance figures create an observable relationship between funding or membership status and stated trading-related balances or paid bonus results.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish how bonuses are calculated, whether they are withdrawable, whether returns are guaranteed, or whether the displayed figures are real account outcomes.

visual_context_notes.observation: The interface includes menu items such as Dashboard, Profile, Pool Account, My Bonus Report, Wallet Section, Team Details, Referral Link, Downline Registration, and Policy Section.
The final slide says “QUESTIONS Please contact the person who sent you this video.”

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it guides viewers to register for and fund a branded trading account by providing identity information and sending Bitcoin, then submitting payment proof. It associates confirmed funding with paid-member status and trading bonuses or results, making the video's own financial solicitation return-related. The material does not establish actual deposits, withdrawals, losses, or the service's legitimacy.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central content explains funding a trading pool account and viewing recurring statements reporting trading results, which supports an investment-pool or managed-trading-return mechanism. The registration flow also requests identity documentation, and the account interface presents sponsor teams, referrals, and binary bonuses.
